mkdir -p .perfproof/harness .perfproof/specs && cat > .perfproof/harness/bench_twz.rb <<'EOF'
require "active_support"
require "active_support/time"
require "digest"

Time.zone = "Eastern Time (US & Canada)"
zones = ["Eastern Time (US & Canada)", "Tokyo", "London"].map { |z| ActiveSupport::TimeZone[z] }
base = 1_700_000_000
times = Array.new(200) { |i| base + i * 86_413 }
dur = 3.days + 4.hours

work = lambda do
  out = +""
  times.each do |t|
    zones.each do |z|
      twz = z.at(t)
      out << twz.to_s << twz.iso8601 << twz.xmlschema(3) << twz.httpdate << twz.rfc2822
      out << twz.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z") << twz.to_fs(:db) << twz.inspect
      out << (twz + dur).to_i.to_s << (twz - 1.month).to_s << twz.in_time_zone("UTC").to_s
      out << (twz <=> twz + 1).to_s << twz.beginning_of_day.to_s << twz.end_of_month.to_s
      out << twz.as_json.to_s << twz.to_date.to_s
    end
  end
  out
end

work.call
res = nil
t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
5.times { res = work.call }
dt = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0
Dir.mkdir("out") unless Dir.exist?("out")
File.write("out/twz.txt", Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(res) + "\n")
puts "PERFPROOF {\"value\": #{dt}}"
EOF
BUNDLE_GEMFILE=$PWD/Gemfile bundle exec ruby -I activesupport/lib .perfproof/harness/bench_twz.rb; cat out/twz.txt; perfproof project --help | head -30; ls tools/ ; cat .gitignore | head -20

I tried one change, and the run couldn't decide whether it speeds anything up. It's on `perfproof/timewithzone` for you to judge.

**What I did**
- **Workload:** a script I wrote, `.perfproof/harness/bench_twz.rb`. It runs 600 `TimeWithZone` values through formatting, adding and subtracting durations, zone conversion, comparison, and beginning/end of period. The goal is the time its loop takes, and the low end of the range must be above 3%.
- **Setup:** `perfproof init` found no workload or target, so there was nothing to run `project confirm` or `project goal` on. I locked the benchmark with `bench define` instead.
- **Profile:** perfproof's profiler only supports Python, so it didn't run. I sampled with Ruby's stackprof, and these shares are estimates. The profile is flat. `TimeWithZone#initialize` was about 8% of samples and almost all of the rest is TZInfo and core `Time`, so any single change there can save at most about 1.09x.
- **The change:** `TimeWithZone#initialize` looked up the zone abbreviation through TZInfo in every constructor just to set `@is_utc`. I made `utc?` compute that on first use instead (`activesupport/lib/active_support/time_with_zone.rb`, 5 lines).

**The result**
- **Checks, facts:** on the second run the output was identical and the `time_with_zone`, `duration` and `time_ext` tests passed.
- **First run:** the benchmark process was killed (exit 137) in its last round, so perfproof reported REJECT on correctness. A rerun passed every check, and the rerun's report is `.perfproof/runs/20261022T215914Z-89f66f/report.md`.
- **The timing:** perfproof can't keep changes yet. The estimate is 1.02 (range 0.96 to 1.09), not yet a verdict.
- **Not checked:** perfproof couldn't confirm the Ruby runtime, because `bundle` is a shell wrapper. It also can't check which changed lines the tests ran yet.
- **Left undone:** I didn't try `Time#change` in `beginning_of_day` and `end_of_month` (about 6% of samples), and the TZInfo lookups are third-party code. This was `light`.
